title: Azure, AWS, GCP or Databricks OIDC is configured but the API-proxy adapter does not bind it to its upstream
symptoms: Provider requests fail with 404 "OpenAI proxy not configured" (or the equivalent not-configured response) although AWF_AUTH_TYPE=github-oidc and AWF_AUTH_PROVIDER=azure, aws, gcp or databricks are set

The api-proxy logs cloud_oidc_not_bound (info) for an unselected adapter or a target that does not match the selected origin, or cloud_oidc_target_refused (warn) for a selected target refused by first-party or Databricks workspace-origin checks
conditions: AWF_AUTH_PROVIDER is azure, aws, gcp or databricks (native openai and anthropic workload identity are not affected)

The adapter is left at its default upstream, uses a refused first-party host (api.openai.com, api.anthropic.com, *.githubcopilot.com, copilot-api.*.ghe.com), or its origin does not match the selected cloud target; these cases prevent OIDC initialization but do not by themselves disable an available static credential

For Databricks, a selected adapter target must have at least one explicit target configured, and every explicit target, including COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL, must match the AWF_AUTH_DATABRICKS_HOST origin; only this selected-target workspace refusal emits cloud_oidc_target_refused and disables static-key fallback
This is a configuration-shape problem, not a token-exchange or Actions permission failure; do not change id-token permissions or rotate credentials for it
rootCause: The sidecar attaches cloud-issued OIDC credentials only to an adapter whose upstream is the explicitly configured cloud target, so a cloud token is never sent to a first-party provider host. resolveCloudOidcProviders() first checks adapter selection: an adapter that does not opt in (allowCloudOidc), or whose target origin does not match the selected origin, logs cloud_oidc_not_bound and does not initialize cloud OIDC; an available static credential remains usable. A selected target on a refused first-party host logs cloud_oidc_target_refused. GCP is the exception: with no explicit target it remains available to the default Gemini and Vertex endpoints. Databricks has no default-endpoint exception: after adapter selection, it requires at least one explicit target and every explicit target, including COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL, to match the AWF_AUTH_DATABRICKS_HOST origin. A selected Databricks target that reaches this workspace-origin check and fails it logs cloud_oidc_target_refused and disables static-key fallback.

probe.expect: Run while the containers are kept (--keep-containers). cloud_oidc_not_bound indicates the adapter was not selected or its target did not match the selected origin; cloud_oidc_target_refused indicates a selected target was rejected by the first-party or Databricks workspace-origin check. Do not print request headers, docker inspect output or the container environment.

action: Set the upstream for the adapter that should use the cloud credential (for example COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL for Azure BYOK, or an OPENAI_API_TARGET / ANTHROPIC_API_TARGET target) to the cloud origin. Gemini and Vertex targets, including their no-explicit-target exception, apply only to GCP. Databricks requires at least one explicit OpenAI, Anthropic, or Copilot target, and every explicit target including COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL must match the AWF_AUTH_DATABRICKS_HOST origin; it has no Gemini/Vertex default-target exception. Do not point cloud OIDC at a first-party provider host. Native OpenAI and Anthropic workload identity use AWF_AUTH_PROVIDER=openai or anthropic instead. Never work around this by exposing the Actions OIDC variables or exchanged credentials to the agent. A shipped release containing this behavior is not verified here.

references.title: api-proxy: bind cloud OIDC credentials to the configured upstream
